metadata.description: `site.toml` — what the registry builder is told before it reads anything (PROP-057 `##SITE-TWO-SOURCES`, campaign atom A5.1). Two sources in the form of a project's `[[registry]]`, and one `[site]` table for the domain the render is for. It is authored data, written once beside the deploy and read by a `vibe` that is rebuilt from `main` far more often than the file changes — which is why it is inventoried and versioned like `maintenance/reviews.toml` rather than left as an untyped config. Nothing secret belongs in it: every source the site reads is read anonymously, so there is no `auth`, no `token_env` and no place to put a credential (campaign rule R-12). Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_site_config/`.
Where the site reads packages from. Absent means a build with no sources, which is refused rather than rendered as an empty site.
The domain this render is for. Absent means every value takes its default, which is the public site.

The two sources of `##SITE-TWO-SOURCES`, each in the form the project's `[[registry]]` already has: a package registry whose index is the change feed, and the host's source repository, which is read as a checkout on disk (`##SITE-HOST-CHECKOUT`).

`[[source.registry]]` — one block per registry, in the order they are polled. The wave ships one (`##SITE-SOURCE-REGISTRY` says «one, by default the GitHub organisation vibespecs»); the table is repeatable because mirrors and second registries are the declared future and a repeatable table does not have to be invented twice.
`[source.host]` — the host's own repository. Absent means this render carries no host.
One package registry, in the shape of a `[[registry]]` block of `vibe.toml` minus everything that authenticates: the site reads every source anonymously.
The local alias, as in `[[registry]].name`. It names the registry in reports and in the builder's state file, so a queue row says which feed it came from.
The organisation-root URL, as in `[[registry]].url` — `https://github.com/vibespecs`.

Where this registry's index lives (PROP-005 §2.2), as in `[[registry]].index_url`. Absent means the default `<url>/index`; the exact value `none` switches the index off, and a site with no index has no change feed to read.

The convention mapping a coordinate to a repository name, as in `[[registry]].naming`: `fqdn`, `kind-name`, `name` or `kind/name`. Typed as a string rather than as an enum of its own so the one vocabulary stays `vibe_core::manifest::NamingConvention` — a second enumeration on the wire would be a second law about what a registry is called. Absent means the default `fqdn`.

The host's source repository (`##SITE-SOURCE-HOST`). The host root is a `[project]` and not a publishable package, so it is not fetched: the deploy keeps a checkout on disk and the renderer reads it (`##SITE-HOST-CHECKOUT`). `git` is therefore an identity — which repository this checkout is of, printed in reports and never cloned by the build.
The repository the checkout is of — `https://github.com/vibevm/vibevm`. Identity, not a fetch instruction.
The branch whose current state is rendered. Absent means `main`; the host has no release tags and the release is what `main` holds now (`##SITE-SOURCE-HOST`).

The directory the deploy keeps the checkout in, relative to this file when relative. Absent means the directory this file sits in, which is what a renderer image that ships its config beside its checkout wants.

How long a render of the host is left alone after it succeeded, however often the branch moves. Absent means 60 — once an hour, the recommended default of `##SITE-HOST-POLL` pending the owner's word (campaign fork F-35), and above the render cost the phase-0 spike measured.
`[site]` — the domain the render is for. Every value has a default, so a configuration that names only its sources builds the public site.
The path the documentation is mounted at. Absent means `/doc` (`##SITE-MOUNT`).

Scheme and host with no trailing slash. Absent means `https://vibevm.org`. It is a default and never a constant: `canonical`, `hreflang` and the sitemap are absolute addresses, and a fork builds this same source for somewhere else.
Which theme a first-time reader gets: `system`, `light` or `dark`. Absent means `system` — the reader's own setting, which is where campaign fork F-48 leaves it until the design review.

The documentations the front of the site shows first, as `<group>/<name>` coordinates without a version — the version shown is whichever one the site serves as `latest`. It is an editorial choice about a domain and belongs to the deployment, which is why it is here and not in any package: no author may feature their own documentation by declaring something. A coordinate no source publishes is a WARNING in the build report and never a refusal, because the registry moves without this file and a deploy must not stop over a package that was renamed.
The first-party analytics property (D-24). Absent means no tag at all.

The self-hosted, cookie-less analytics tag the landing already carries (`##SITE-ANALYTICS`). Both values identify a live property, so they belong to the deployment and not to the repository; empty is the instruction «publish nothing», never a hole for whoever notices.
The property id. Empty or absent renders no tag at all — not a tag with an empty attribute, which would load the script and report nothing.
Where the tag reports to. Absent means the site's own origin, which is what a first-party tag served by the domain itself reports to.
